t: Officers who had seen the Napoleonic Wars and the suffering of peasant soldiers formed secret societies from 1816, seeking a constitution and the end of serfdom.
In the confusion after Alexander I’s death in 1825 they led about 3,000 troops into Senate Square in Saint Petersburg, where loyal troops broke them with grapeshot at the end of the day.
Five leaders were hanged and many exiled to Siberia, where the Decembrists founded schools and brought new crops, and their wives’ devotion made the word Dekabristka a Russian symbol.
dyk: The rising failed partly because its chosen leader, Prince Sergei Trubetskoy, deserted it on the day, and his second-in-command, Colonel Bulatov, also vanished from the scene; the rebels had to appoint Prince Eugene Obolensky in a hurried consultation.
ev: Officers of the Imperial Russian Guard found the Union of Salvation, which takes a revolutionary turn when Pavel Pestel joins it
After a mutiny in the Semenovsky Regiment, the society suspends activity, but a Northern and a Southern Society carry on in secret
The Society of United Slavs is founded in Novohrad-Volynsky, seeking an equal federation of Slavic peoples
Alexander I dies suddenly, and parts of the army swear loyalty to Konstantin, unaware that he has renounced the throne
About 3,000 rebel troops refuse the oath to Nicholas I in Senate Square, Saint Petersburg, and are scattered by artillery
The Chernigov Regiment, led by Sergey Muravyov-Apostol, rises in Ukraine and is defeated within five days
The first party of Decembrist convicts sets out for Siberia, bound for the mines at Nerchinsk
On the accession of Alexander II the Decembrists are amnestied and their rights restored

f.where: the Russian Empire: Saint Petersburg, where the Northern Society met and the rising took place in Senate Square; Tulchin and Vasylkiv in Ukraine, centres of the Southern Society; Novohrad-Volynsky, where the Society of United Slavs was founded; afterwards places of exile across Siberia
f.period: Union of Salvation from 1816; Union of Prosperity, suspended in 1821; Northern and Southern Societies 1821–1825; Society of United Slavs from 1823; the rising in Senate Square in December 1825; the Chernigov Regiment’s revolt in January 1826; trial and exile from 1826; amnesty 1856
f.figures: Pavel Pestel, radical leader of the Southern Society; Nikita Muravyov, author of a constitution; Prince Sergei Trubetskoy, chosen as interim ruler, who deserted the rising; Prince Eugene Obolensky, who took his place; Sergey Muravyov-Apostol, leader of the revolt in Ukraine; Pyotr Kakhovsky; Maria Volkonskaya, who followed her husband into exile
f.outcome: crushed by artillery in Saint Petersburg and in Ukraine; five leaders hanged and many others imprisoned or exiled to Siberia; the autocracy continued for almost a century, but the revolt has been considered the beginning of a revolutionary movement in Russia
